description_ru: Двое старых друзей встречаются спустя двенадцать лет, и невозвращённый долг оказывается важнее самих денег. Разговор о стыде, молчании и дружбе.
text:
Nadia: Callum! Look at you. You've gone grey in precisely the distinguished way I always said you would.
Callum: And you've gone completely unchanged, which is infuriating. Twelve years, Nadia. Twelve. When did we last see each other?
Nadia: Your wedding, I think. You were crying during the speeches, and you denied it for a decade.
Callum: It was hay fever. In a marquee. In June.
Nadia: Of course it was. The marquee was spotless, and you were the only man in the tent with a handkerchief, which I always thought rather telling. Come on, let's get a drink before the awkward part of the reunion begins, the part where everybody asks what everybody does.

Callum: Too late. I've already been asked by three people, and one of them thought I was my brother.
Nadia: Poor you. Well, I'll save you the trouble. I run a restaurant. Two, actually, as of March. The second one is in Lyon, which is faintly absurd, as I can barely order a coffee in French.
Callum: That is wonderful. I mean it. I always thought you would do something exuberant with your life, though I assumed it would involve fire.
Nadia: And you? Please don't tell me you went into insurance.

Callum: Pensions, which is worse. I spend my days explaining to people in their thirties that they'll be old one day, and watching them look at me as though I'd suggested they might die.
Nadia: Which is, technically, what you're suggesting.
Callum: I prefer to call it long-term planning. It sounds less like a threat. But it pays for a house, a dog, and a daughter who is currently convinced she's going to be a marine biologist, a poet, or possibly a pirate.
Nadia: A sensible mixture. I'd back her.
Callum: I'll tell her you said so. She'll want a reference.

Nadia: There's a great deal of fire. Mostly accidental. But listen, Callum, there's something I need to say, and I've rehearsed it on the train, so please don't interrupt.
Callum: That sounds ominous. You haven't taken up politics, have you?
Nadia: Worse. I've taken up honesty, and my therapist says it's going well.
Callum: Then I'm properly frightened.

Nadia: It's about the money.
Callum: Which money?
Nadia: Don't pretend. The four thousand pounds you lent me in the spring of two thousand and twelve, when the first restaurant was about to go under and every bank in the country had laughed me out of the building.
Callum: Ah. That money.
Nadia: I never paid it back.

Callum: I'd noticed, yes.
Nadia: And I never said anything, which is the part I'm properly ashamed of. I told myself I'd do it when I was solvent. Then I was solvent, and I told myself it would be strange to bring it up after so long. Then it became a kind of elephant, and I started avoiding your messages, and eventually the friendship simply withered because I was too much of a coward to mention a debt.
Callum: Nadia, stop. Let me say something, since you've had your turn.
Nadia: Go on. I deserve whatever you say.

Callum: I knew exactly what had happened, and I was quietly furious for about two years. Then my daughter was born, and I stopped having the energy for resentment. By the time I had enough energy back, I'd decided I missed you more than I wanted the cash.
Nadia: That's much too generous.
Callum: It isn't generous, it's practical. Money you can earn again. Friends are a good deal harder to replace.
Nadia: You make it sound so simple.
Callum: It rarely is, but it's occasionally simpler than we fear. I wish I'd learned that earlier.

Nadia: Well, I have it with me. Here. It's in an envelope, which I realise is theatrical.
Callum: It's four thousand pounds in an envelope. You've turned a reunion into a film scene.
Nadia: And there's interest. I worked out the interest. Look, I even used a spreadsheet.
Callum: A spreadsheet. I'm genuinely moved. But I can't take it, you know.

Nadia: Of course you can. It's yours.
Callum: Then let me take the principal and refuse the interest, on the condition that you spend the difference on something ridiculous. Or better still, on a meal. I've never eaten in either of your restaurants, and I'm told the one in Lyon has an excellent reputation for being impossible to book.
Nadia: For you, the table is always free, and I'll bring out the dessert myself. It involves flames, naturally.
Callum: Naturally. I'll bring my daughter, if that's all right. She's nine, and she's been told that a restaurant is a place where adults pretend they aren't hungry.
Nadia: Then I'll cook her something enormous, and she can pretend with pleasure. But go on, you said hold on.

Callum: So I did. But hold on, really. Honestly, this next part is difficult. There's something I also owe you, and it's a matter of pride rather than money.
Nadia: You owe me nothing.
Callum: I do, and I'd like to say it plainly. When you rang that spring, I made you wait three days for an answer. I told myself I was being careful. The truth is that I was embarrassed, because I'd half hoped you'd ask someone else. I resented being asked, and then I resented myself for resenting it. If I'd been a better friend, I'd have said yes immediately, and perhaps you wouldn't have felt so much shame afterwards.
Nadia: I never knew that.

Callum: It seems we've both been keeping silent for twelve years out of misplaced delicacy. We're a pair of idiots.
Nadia: Distinguished idiots. One of us is grey.
Callum: And one of us is solvent. I propose a toast. To awkward conversations, long overdue.
Nadia: And to the hay fever, which has served us both so faithfully.
Callum: You are the only person alive who gets away with that.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: В слове withered середина — звонкое «ð»: язык между зубами, голос включён, и только потом краткое «ə».
Ударение: exˈuberant, theˈatrical, emˈbarrassed. Второй слог ударный, а первый почти исчезает.
«v» — зубы касаются нижней губы, голос звучит: twelve, give. Не заменяйте на «ф» или «в» с губами.
Конечные звонкие согласные (said, ashamed) не оглушайте; удлиняйте предшествующий гласный.

questions.question: When did Callum and Nadia last meet?
questions.answer: At Callum's wedding twelve years ago.

questions.question: What had Nadia not done for twelve years?
questions.answer: She had not repaid the four thousand pounds Callum lent her.

questions.question: How does Callum feel about the debt?
questions.answer: He was furious for two years, but then decided he missed her more than the money.

questions.question: What does Callum confess?
questions.answer: He had made her wait three days and was embarrassed and resentful about being asked.
